product.name: AI Atlas
product.description: A finite route through the detailed roadmap and the resource library.

coreMap.title: Mathematical Foundations
coreMap.summary: Linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics and optimization for reasoning about models.

coreMap.title: Programming & Software Engineering
coreMap.summary: Python execution, interfaces, testing, debugging, Linux and reproducibility.

coreMap.title: Algorithms & Data Structures
coreMap.summary: Invariants, complexity, structures, graphs, dynamic programming and transfer.

coreMap.title: Classical Machine Learning
coreMap.summary: Formulation, models, evaluation, uncertainty, shift and experimentation.

coreMap.title: Deep Learning
coreMap.summary: Autograd, training dynamics, architectures, representation learning and reliability.

coreMap.title: Systems Foundations
coreMap.summary: Operating systems, concurrency, networking, storage, reliability and security.

coreMap.title: LLM Foundations
coreMap.summary: Tokenization, transformers, pretraining, evaluation and KV-cached generation.

advancedTracks.title: Applied Science & ML Research
advancedTracks.summary: Turn an ambiguous ML question into a falsifiable formulation, fair comparison, trustworthy experiment and defensible decision. One investigation grows across the track, preserving uncertainty, negative evidence and reproducible lineage.

sections.title: Falsifiable Formulation
sections.why: A useful investigation begins with a decision, a measurable claim and evidence that could prove the proposed explanation wrong. This stage fixes that contract before model choice can hide a weak question.

topics.title: Problem context, stakeholders and the decision that may change
Decision, prediction and causal questions as distinct formulations
User action, intervention and outcome horizon
Population, unit, target and estimand
Feature time, label time and action time
Constructs, proxy metrics and construct validity
Utility, error cost, operational constraints and guardrails
Mechanism hypothesis and predicted observable signatures
Falsification conditions and competing explanations
Smallest useful effect and practical significance
Deploy, iterate, collect-data and stop thresholds
Naive, heuristic, simple learned and strongest reasonable baselines
Split, metric and evaluation contract fixed before comparison
Baseline-only study of variance, slices, difficulty and headroom
Failure tree across data, model, metric, causal, system and product causes
Data rights, privacy, safety, compute and feasibility boundaries
Value-of-information ranking for candidate experiments
Formal utility and Bayesian decision theory
Full causal identification analysis

resources.name: Project Design - Planning and Checklist
resources.use: Use Getting Started with Project Design, the Getting Started Checklist and Reproducibility Methods. Record users, methods, resources, risks, ethics, expected outcomes and which work is exploratory or confirmatory.

resources.name: Machine Learning Problem Framing
resources.use: Complete Understand the Problem, Frame the ML Problem and Summary with every embedded exercise. Convert the result into a one-page contract naming the decision, output, data, metric, benchmark and non-ML alternative.

resources.name: The Heilmeier Catechism
resources.use: Answer all eight questions for the proposed investigation, including current practice, novelty, who cares, risks, cost, duration and the midterm and final examinations. Use the answers to remove vague scope.

resources.name: Rules of Machine Learning - Selected Rules
resources.use: Read the opening, Rules 1-5, Rule 12 and Rules 25-28. Use them to preserve a simple baseline, define the first pipeline and anticipate metric and error-pattern failures. Do not read all 43 rules now.

resources.name: CS329S - Machine Learning Systems Design
resources.use: Use the lectures Understanding ML Production, Training Data, Model Selection and Development, Model Training and Offline Evaluation. Extract operational constraints and failure modes into the problem contract.

resources.name: Applied Science Investigation - Research Charter
resources.use: Use Overview, Milestone A and the correctness requirements as the artifact template. Begin one investigation here and keep extending the same artifact through AS-8.

sections.checkpoint: Defend three formulations for one ambiguous request, select one, and show an executable baseline contract with timing and leakage tests plus a result that would falsify the proposed mechanism.
leaveForLater: Full causal identification and policy optimization
Production feature-store and monitoring architecture
Formal decision theory beyond the chosen decision

sections.title: Statistical Learning Judgment
sections.why: Model choice is a scientific comparison problem. This stage teaches how to match inductive bias to data and decision constraints while preventing tuning effort, seed choice or leakage from deciding the winner.

topics.title: Empirical risk, expected risk and generalization
Hypothesis classes and inductive bias
Capacity, complexity and regularization
Bias-variance tradeoff and its observable signatures
Irreducible, approximation, estimation, optimization and distribution error
Model family choice from data, decision and operational constraints
Nested model selection and final-test isolation
Preprocessing and feature selection inside the selection loop
Matched tuning, compute and wall-clock budgets
Complete seed retention and no best-seed filtering
Learning curves and validation curves for diagnosis
Calibration, recalibration and decision thresholds
Abstention and selective risk-coverage behavior
Ensembles, diversity and correlated errors
Data intervention versus model intervention
Residual, shortcut, counterfactual and slice diagnosis
Bayesian prior sensitivity for high-cost decisions
PAC bounds and uniform convergence proofs
Bayesian model averaging and posterior predictive comparison
Large automated hyperparameter sweeps

resources.name: STATS202 - Data Mining and Analysis
resources.use: Follow Introduction, Regression, Classification, Resampling, Model Selection, Tree-Based Methods, SVM and Unsupervised Learning in that order. Complete the matching public labs and prediction challenge workflow.

resources.name: An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Python
resources.use: Use Chapters 2-9 and 12 only where STATS202 needs a second explanation or lab. Prioritize the end-of-chapter labs for resampling, model selection, trees, SVM and unsupervised learning.

resources.name: CS229 Public Materials - Learning Theory and Model Selection
resources.use: Read notes4 on learning theory, notes5 on regularization and model selection, and the practical advice material. Use them to defend capacity, regularization and fair selection without repeating the full core ML course.

resources.name: Deep Learning Tuning Playbook - Scientific Tuning
resources.use: Read the scientific approach, incremental tuning, exploration versus exploitation, scientific and nuisance hyperparameters, and study-design sections. Predeclare fair budgets and retain every valid run.

resources.name: scikit-learn - Model Selection and Evaluation
resources.use: Implement nested cross-validation, learning curves and validation curves from the linked examples. Add a test that fails if preprocessing or selection sees the final test fold.

resources.name: scikit-learn - Probability Calibration Examples
resources.use: Run the calibration-curve and classifier-calibration examples. Compare ranking, probability quality and the downstream decision after calibration instead of reporting accuracy alone.

sections.checkpoint: Run a matched-budget comparison of two materially different model families. The ranking must survive reasonable seed and budget changes, and the report must isolate whether the next gain is more likely to come from data or model complexity.
leaveForLater: Full proofs of statistical learning theory
Bayesian model averaging and advanced posterior computation
Large search services and population-based tuning

sections.title: Measurement and Uncertainty
sections.why: A model result is useful only when the measurement matches the sampling process and the remaining uncertainty is visible. This stage turns scores into decisions without hiding dependence, multiplicity or practical cost.

topics.title: Internal, external, construct and statistical-conclusion validity
Sampling unit, dependence and pseudoreplication
Estimand, estimator and effect size
Sampling distributions and standard errors
Confidence intervals and repeated-sampling interpretation
Credible intervals and prior-dependent interpretation
Bootstrap at the correct resampling unit
Permutation and randomization tests
Null, alternative, test statistic and reference distribution
Type I and II errors, power and minimum detectable effect
Optional stopping and sequential looks
Multiple outcomes, slices, comparisons and adjustments
Pre-analysis plan, exclusions and deviation log
Seed, data, annotator and system variance
Robust aggregation, distributions and sensitivity analysis
Heterogeneous effects, slice counts and stability
Calibration, sharpness and limits of aggregate ECE
Prediction intervals and conformal coverage
Selective risk, coverage and abstention
Semiparametric efficiency and always-valid inference
Formal asymptotic theory beyond the selected estimator

resources.name: MS&E 226 - Fundamentals of Data Science
resources.use: Study Lectures 8-12 on frequentist inference, standard errors, confidence intervals, bootstrap, hypothesis testing and multiple tests, then Lecture 16 on Bayesian inference and decision making. Complete the linked notebooks or apps.

resources.name: SciPy Statistics - Resampling and Monte Carlo Methods
resources.use: Complete the Monte Carlo test, permutation test and bootstrap tutorials. Rebuild one interval or test from blank NumPy code and validate its behavior under a null and a known effect.

resources.name: statsmodels - Power and Multiple Testing
resources.use: Use the power and sample-size classes plus multipletests for the chosen experiment. Record the assumed effect and variance, then test sensitivity to plausible misspecification.

resources.name: MAPIE - Prediction Sets and Intervals
resources.use: Use the quick start for one regression interval or classification prediction set. Check empirical coverage overall and by a predeclared slice, then report interval width or set size.

resources.name: 18.650 - Statistics for Applications
resources.use: Use selected lectures and problem sets on parametric inference, maximum likelihood, hypothesis testing, Bayesian statistics and generalized linear models when the investigation needs more derivation than MS&E 226 supplies.

resources.name: Applied Science and ML Research Checkpoint
resources.use: Use the Formulate and Reason plus Reproduce and Experiment sections as the closed-note audit for sampling units, uncertainty, robustness and decision language.

sections.checkpoint: Execute a precommitted analysis with the correct sampling and resampling units. Demonstrate by simulation that a naive analysis can mislead, then defend the repaired decision using effect, uncertainty, cost and validity threats.
leaveForLater: Sequential and always-valid inference theory
Semiparametric efficiency and influence functions
Hierarchical Bayesian modeling beyond the chosen investigation

sections.title: Data-Centric Science and Shift
sections.why: The dataset is part of the mechanism, not a neutral input. This stage makes provenance, coverage, label policy, leakage, shift and feedback measurable before another model iteration is allowed.

topics.title: Provenance, license, consent, privacy and permitted use
Schema, units, ranges and semantic contracts
MCAR, MAR and MNAR as diagnostic models
Annotation instructions, disagreement and adjudication
Label-error detection and confident-learning intuition
Class imbalance, rare events and metric consequences
Outliers, hard negatives and boundary coverage
Exact duplicates, near duplicates and benchmark contamination
Sampling, population coverage and long-tail behavior
Predeclared slice taxonomy and sparse-slice uncertainty
Fairness metrics, label bias and subgroup harm boundaries
Covariate, label and concept shift
Observed drift versus measured performance degradation
Delayed labels, detection delay and monitoring blind spots
Fixed-model relabeling, filtering, deduplication and coverage studies
Active selection and information value of new labels
Synthetic-data amplification, collapse and provenance risks
Feedback loops, selective labels and retraining bias
Data lineage, transformation state and version manifest
Advanced fairness-constrained optimization
Differential privacy and privacy-preserving learning
Large-scale annotation and data-governance platforms

resources.name: Introduction to Data-Centric AI
resources.use: Follow the 2024 lectures and labs on data-centric versus model-centric development, label errors, imbalance, outliers, distribution shift, dataset creation, curation and evaluation. Use the GenAI curation unit only if the chosen artifact is generative.

resources.name: Data Governance for the ML Pipeline
resources.use: Read Data Governance for the ML Pipeline, Version Control for Data and Data Cleaning. Record ownership, consent, access, deletion, transformations, fitted state, quality checks and immutable identifiers.

resources.name: Data Cards Playbook - User Guide
resources.use: Complete the eight-step workflow. Produce a compact data card covering authorship, intent, access, deletion, provenance, sensitive attributes, transformations, annotations, sampling, validation and known uses.

resources.name: scikit-learn - Common Pitfalls
resources.use: Study inconsistent preprocessing and data leakage. Convert the examples into tests for split overlap, future features, preprocessing scope, duplicate entities and fitted-state leakage.

resources.name: ML Crash Course - Production ML Systems
resources.use: Use the production systems unit for data dependencies, feedback loops and monitoring. Apply its exercises to the artifact's delayed labels, drift signals and retraining boundary.

resources.name: ML Crash Course - Fairness
resources.use: Use the fairness unit for sources of bias, subgroup evaluation and metric choice. Apply only the exercises needed to state and measure the artifact's fairness boundary.

resources.name: Applied Science Investigation - Data Audit
resources.use: Use Milestones B and E plus the failure-injection list for provenance, leakage, duplicates, shift, subgroup sparsity and data-lineage evidence.

sections.checkpoint: Trace every reported example to a versioned data and label process, then run at least three fixed-model data interventions and a controlled-shift test with uncertainty, slice effects, detection delay and an explicit retraining decision.
leaveForLater: Advanced fairness optimization and causal fairness
Differential privacy and federated data governance
Large annotation operations and production data platforms

sections.title: Causal Reasoning and Online Experiments
sections.why: Prediction, association and intervention answer different questions. This stage establishes the minimum causal reasoning and experiment-integrity discipline needed to make deployment claims safely.

topics.title: Potential outcomes and ATE, ATT and CATE estimands
Consistency, exchangeability and overlap assumptions
SUTVA, interference and treatment leakage
Causal DAGs as assumption maps
Confounders, colliders, mediators and post-treatment variables
Identification and valid adjustment sets
Prediction, association and intervention claims
Randomization unit and analysis unit
Blocking, stratification and variance reduction
Cluster randomization and dependent outcomes
Power, precision and smallest useful effect
Assignment, exposure, outcome and exclusion logs
Sample-ratio mismatch and experiment-integrity diagnosis
Guardrails, staged ramp and rollback
Novelty, seasonality and carryover effects
Sequential monitoring without post hoc threshold changes
Heterogeneous effects with predeclared slices
Matching, weighting and regression adjustment boundaries
Sensitivity to unmeasured confounding and alternative specifications
Natural experiments and quasi-experimental designs
Longitudinal g-methods and time-varying confounding
Always-valid inference for continuous experimentation

resources.name: Causal Inference: What If
resources.use: Read Chapters 1-3 for causal effects without models and Chapters 6-8 for causal diagrams, confounding, selection and identification. Reproduce one associated code example and label every assumption.

resources.name: 14.310x - Data Analysis for Social Scientists
resources.use: Revisit Weeks 7, 9 and 10 for randomized experiments, omitted-variable bias, endogeneity, instrumental variables and experimental design. Complete one design problem and one analysis problem.

resources.name: Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation - Pre-Experiment
resources.use: Use the pre-experiment checks to lock hypotheses, metrics, randomization, power, telemetry, guardrails and ramp criteria before outcomes are inspected.

resources.name: Patterns of Trustworthy Experimentation - During Experiment
resources.use: Use the during-experiment checks for assignment, exposure, data quality, novelty, guardrails and staged ramp. Keep integrity checks separate from effect estimation.

resources.name: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in A/B Testing
resources.use: Implement an SRM check and a diagnosis tree. Seed one assignment or telemetry defect and resolve it before estimating the treatment effect.

resources.name: Causal Inference: The Mixtape
resources.use: Use selected chapters on DAGs, experiments and matching only if the What If presentation does not make the design boundary clear. It is an alternate explanation, not a second required spine.

sections.checkpoint: Simulate confounding, collider adjustment, post-treatment selection and interference, then defend an online experiment plan with correct units, power or precision, telemetry, SRM checks, guardrails, ramp, stopping and rollback.
leaveForLater: Longitudinal causal inference and mediation
Semiparametric causal estimators
Always-valid inference infrastructure for continuous experimentation

sections.title: Reproduction, Ablation and Scaling
sections.why: Research claims often collapse under implementation differences, evaluator changes or unequal resources. This stage turns a paper claim into a tested mechanism with complete lineage, controlled ablations and explicit scale boundaries.

topics.title: Claim decomposition into mechanism, assumptions and evidence
Equation-to-code and claim-to-output traceability
Environment, data, evaluator and protocol equivalence
Predeclared reproduction tolerance and equivalence criteria
Baseline fidelity and matched resource budgets
Clean-room reproduction from documented artifacts
Discrepancy log and unresolved-difference boundary
All-run, all-seed and failed-run retention
Mechanism invariants, parity tests and negative tests
Scientific, nuisance and fixed experimental factors
One-factor and small factorial ablation designs
Interaction effects and non-additive ablations
Minimum mechanism-isolating ablation matrix
Negative controls and placebo interventions
Compute, data, precision, hardware and system matching
Scaling curves, resource normalization and uncertainty
Interpolation, extrapolation and regime boundaries
Robustness, out-of-distribution and stress tests
Null, negative and contradictory evidence
Immutable raw results, environment and analysis manifests
Hyperparameter transfer across scale
Formal scaling-law estimation and uncertainty
Frontier-scale distributed replication

resources.name: The Turing Way - Reproducible Research
resources.use: Read the overview, Version Control for Data, Testing, Reproducible Environments and Research Compendia. Build a clean reproduction bundle containing code, data, configuration, environment, hardware, raw outputs, failures and analysis version.

resources.name: Deep Learning Tuning Playbook - Experiment Design
resources.use: Use the sections on scientific, nuisance and fixed hyperparameters, designing studies, extracting insights, evaluation and experiment tracking. Turn each ablation into a stated question rather than a sweep.

resources.name: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
resources.use: Audit experimental details, statistical claims, compute, data, code and reproducibility before accepting a reproduction. Link every answer to an artifact or a clearly stated limitation.

resources.name: PyTorch Reproducibility Notes
resources.use: For neural investigations, control documented randomness sources and deterministic settings, record device and version, and state where exact cross-platform reproducibility is unavailable.

resources.name: How to Scale Your Model
resources.use: Use only the relevant sections on roofline analysis, sharding, transformer math, training, inference, JAX and GPUs. Apply them to resource matching and scale boundaries, not as another systems course.

resources.name: Applied Science Investigation - Reproduction and Ablation
resources.use: Use Milestones C through F, the correctness requirements and failure-injection list as the evidence contract for reproduction, ablations, robustness, lineage and independent regeneration.

sections.checkpoint: Reproduce or rigorously bound one nontrivial claim, then run three mechanism-isolating ablations, one negative control and one robustness or scale-boundary test. Preserve every discrepancy, failed run and null result.
leaveForLater: Frontier-scale distributed reproduction
Formal scaling-law research beyond the selected claim
Large combinatorial or automated ablation sweeps

sections.title: Research Communication and Review
sections.why: A conclusion is only defensible when every claim can be traced to evidence and its strongest limitation is visible. This stage turns the investigation into an auditable report that can survive skeptical review.

topics.title: Claim-evidence ledger with artifact links
Observation, inference, decision and speculation as separate statements
Prior-work and claim matrix
Novelty and contribution boundary
Paper and report structure as an evidence argument
Methods section and locked experiment contract
Results generated from immutable raw artifacts
Figure and table units, denominators, sample counts and uncertainty
Honest axes, scales, aggregation and comparison sets
Ablation narrative tied to the mechanism hypothesis
Limitations, negative evidence and unresolved discrepancies
Artifact README, commands and environment reconstruction
Report-to-code and figure-to-raw-output traceability
Peer review across validity, baselines, statistics and overclaiming
Review-response matrix with evidence and remaining risk
Oral defense of assumptions, alternatives and strongest unsupported inference
Independent clean reproduction of one primary result
Next experiment selected by information gain
Plain-language and stakeholder communication
Venue-specific positioning and rebuttal strategy
Publication formatting and submission operations

resources.name: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
resources.use: Use the checklist while planning and writing. Audit claims, limitations, assumptions, experimental details, statistics, compute, data, code, ethics and societal impact, with every answer linked to a report section or artifact.

resources.name: The Turing Way - Guide for Communication
resources.use: Read the communication overview, wider-audience principles and Research Objects. Produce a technical report, decision memo and plain-language summary that preserve the same claim boundary.

resources.name: NeurIPS 2026 Reviewer Guidelines
resources.use: Structure an adversarial review around quality, clarity, significance and originality. Require three to five actionable objections that could change the conclusion, then answer them with evidence or explicit remaining risk.

resources.name: Journal or Conference Paper CommKit
resources.use: Use the argument, audience, outline and section guidance to convert the evidence ledger into a readable technical paper. Check that each paragraph advances a claim or establishes its boundary.

resources.name: Results and Figure Design CommKits
resources.use: Use the Results guidance and figure-design principles to choose comparisons, expose uncertainty and make every axis, unit, denominator and visual encoding interpretable without hidden context.

resources.name: Artifact Review and Badging
resources.use: Use the current availability, functionality, reproducibility and replicability criteria as an artifact audit. This is a quality target for the bundle, not a requirement to submit it.

sections.checkpoint: Generate the report and every figure from immutable raw results, pass a skeptical review using a claim-evidence response matrix, and have a clean environment or independent person reproduce one primary result.
leaveForLater: Venue-specific formatting and submission operations
Rebuttal tactics beyond an evidence-based response
Publication strategy and research branding

sections.title: Original Research Judgment
sections.why: Research independence is the ability to choose a consequential bounded question, design the smallest decisive study, respond honestly to negative evidence and stop when the remaining claim is not supported.

topics.title: New mechanism, measurement, analysis, negative result and useful combination as contribution types
Problem selection from decision relevance and tractability
Who acts differently under each possible outcome
Prior work, closest claim and precise novelty boundary
Hidden assumptions and strongest competing explanation
Expected information gain of candidate experiments
Feasibility, compute, data, time and skill budget
Technical risk, ethics, misuse and societal-impact boundary
Small portfolio of competing hypotheses
Success, partial, null, contradiction and stop outcomes

Simpler alternative designs and non-ML routes
Independent implementation or material modification of the central mechanism
Exploratory work separated from confirmatory claims
External validity, regime boundary and unsupported transfer
Extend, narrow, revise or stop after negative evidence
Independent reproduction and adversarial review
Strongest unsupported inference stated explicitly

Independent lab leadership and long-horizon agenda setting

resources.name: The Turing Way - Project Design
resources.use: Use Overview, Getting Started with Project Design, the checklist and Reproducibility Methods to define the question, users, methods, resources, risks, governance, communication plan and success criteria before implementation.

resources.name: The Heilmeier Catechism
resources.use: Answer all eight questions for two candidate projects. Reject any proposal that cannot state current practice, novelty, value, risk, resource cost and concrete midterm and final examinations.

resources.name: Registered Reports
resources.use: Use the format to separate question quality from result direction. Write a short preregistration naming success, partial success, null, contradiction and stop outcomes before the decisive experiment.

resources.name: NeurIPS Reviewer Criteria
resources.use: Score two candidate questions for quality, clarity, significance and originality, then audit limitations and unsupported claims. Treat a negative result or new measurement as valid only when the evidence changes understanding.

resources.name: Applied Science Research Laboratory
resources.use: Use the complete capstone contract for the bounded original question, baseline reproduction, preregistered intervention, ablations, failures, independent reproduction, report, review response and oral defense.

resources.name: MLRC 2026 - Reproducibility Track
resources.use: Read the official track announcement only after the local capstone passes. Use it to understand how a rigorous reproduction, replication or negative result can become a public research artifact.

sections.checkpoint: Choose between two bounded questions, preregister the minimum decisive study for one, build or materially modify its central mechanism, and make an extend, narrow, revise or stop decision after independent reproduction and adversarial review.
leaveForLater: Flagship publication as a completion requirement
A multi-project research portfolio
Independent lab leadership and long-horizon agenda setting

milestone.title: Applied Science Investigation
milestone.description: Choose one bounded consequential claim in a domain already covered by the core. Carry the same versioned investigation from formulation through reproduction, controlled experimentation, review and a final research decision.
deliverables: A research charter and clean baseline reproduction with versioned data, code, environment and evaluation manifests, leakage tests and a discrepancy log.
A preregistered matched-budget study with naive and strong baselines, mechanism ablations, a negative control, correct uncertainty, shift and error analysis, and all-attempt retention.
A generated technical report and decision memo with claim-to-artifact links, independent clean reproduction, a skeptical review response and the next smallest decisive experiment.

advancedTracks.title: LLM Research, Training & Post-training
advancedTracks.summary: Design and execute trustworthy language-model training and post-training research from data and architecture through scaling, evaluation, adaptation, preference optimization, reasoning, multimodality and safety. One versioned research program grows across the track and ends in a mechanism-isolating contribution.

sections.title: Data and Tokenizer Systems
sections.why: Language-model behavior begins in the corpus. This stage makes extraction, filtering, deduplication, tokenization, mixing and batch lineage reproducible enough that a model result can be attributed to a real data intervention.

resources.name: CS336 Assignment 4 - Data
resources.use: Complete the offline-sized path through HTML extraction, language identification, PII masking, harmful-content filtering, Gopher-style rules, the quality classifier, exact deduplication and MinHash. Train only the smallest comparison needed to test one data intervention; the 8-B200 leaderboard run is outside this gate.

resources.name: CS336 2026 - Data Lectures 13 and 14
resources.use: Study Lecture 13 on sources and datasets and Lecture 14 on filtering, deduplication, mixing and synthetic data before finalizing the pipeline contract. Reconcile each lecture claim with the Assignment 4 implementation.

resources.name: Dolma Toolkit
resources.use: Read the toolkit overview and inspect extraction, filtering, deduplication, mixing and tokenization configuration. Use it as a real pipeline reference after the CS336 implementation works, and record which production concerns your smaller pipeline omits.

resources.name: Modern LLM Notebook - Data Engineering
resources.use: Work through notebook 15-data-engineering. Reproduce the compact extraction, filtering, deduplication and mixture examples, then compare their assumptions with the stricter CS336 tests.

resources.name: TensorTonic - Data Processing Set
resources.use: Solve Perform Stable Exact Deduplication, Build Deterministic MinHash Signatures and Compute Temperature-Based Data Mixtures. Keep the outputs as unit-tested utilities in the track project.

resources.name: Tokenizer and Corpus Pipeline
resources.use: Reuse the project correctness, lineage and contamination contracts. Extend the artifact instead of starting another tokenizer implementation.

resources.name: DataComp for Language Models
resources.use: Read the baseline paper and inspect the repository only after the bounded data experiment. Use it to study large-scale pool construction and data-selection experiments, not as required infrastructure.

sections.checkpoint: Reproduce an arbitrary training batch from dataset version, seed, shard and position; bound duplicate and evaluation overlap with reviewed evidence; then show a fixed-compute model result for one filtering or mixture intervention.
leaveForLater: Full-corpus Common Crawl processing and the CS336 data leaderboard

General-purpose data attribution and active data selection research

milestone.title: Distributed Training Systems Laboratory
milestone.description: Carry one tiny transformer and one evidence repository through the track. Keep correctness runnable on CPU processes, add hardware measurements only where available, and finish with a bounded change to a real training codebase.
deliverables: A correctness core with restartable data and state, rank and group construction, tested collectives, single-process numerical oracles, DDP and sharded steps, TP, CP and PP mechanisms, a tiny MoE dispatcher, structured rank traces and analytic memory and communication models.

A composed-plan and recovery dossier with a legal 2D or 4D device mesh, topology and batch constraints, predicted memory and critical path, atomic sharded checkpoints, changed-layout restore, kill and corruption campaigns, and explicit separation of simulated, CPU, single-GPU and multi-GPU evidence.

A real-code extension in Picotron, TorchFeather, TorchTitan or an isolated Bumblebee branch with a fixed-workload baseline, aligned profiles, correctness and regression tests, before and after throughput, memory and reliability results with variance, a reproducible manifest, negative evidence and a skeptical design defense.

The route revises the fundamentals, then requires deterministic fault histories and a single integrated subsystem whose guarantees remain precise under failure.

milestone.title: Kernel-to-System Performance Laboratory
milestone.description: Carry one transformer operation and one realistic inference workload through a single evidence repository, from arithmetic and benchmark design through CUDA and Triton kernels, compiler and engine integration, communication analysis and a final architecture-aware extension.
deliverables: A correctness-first performance laboratory with hardware and software manifests, independent framework or CPU references, synchronized cold and warm benchmarks, raw interleaved trials, operation and byte models, roofline analysis, Nsight timelines and counters, sanitizer regressions and a repaired misleading benchmark.

A CUDA and Triton kernel suite containing data movement, reduction or scan, stable softmax, tiled GEMM and one attention or fused transformer path; LeetGPU challenge evidence; adversarial shape, stride, dtype, mask, numerical and asynchronous tests; strong library and compiler baselines; autotuning, dispatch and correct fallback; and retained losing regimes.

A real kernel-to-inference or communication integration with TTFT, TPOT, memory, goodput and quality evidence; one reconstructed and modified production kernel, compiler or collective path; held-out and portability tests; a clean reproduction package; claim-to-artifact links; a workload-weighted gain; and an honest negative result.

advancedTracks.title: Reinforcement Learning
advancedTracks.summary: Move through three explicit modules: compact classical control foundations, deeper neural policy and value learning, and an extensive language-model RL route covering feedback, preference objectives, online optimization, reasoning, agents and scalable evaluation.

This stage makes the environment contract, value definitions and planning oracles executable so later learning curves can be checked against something stronger than apparent reward improvement.

sections.title: Linear Algebra & Proof
sections.why: Models are compositions of linear maps. Geometry, rank and conditioning explain what a model can represent and when a correct formula still fails numerically.

topics.title: Definitions, quantifiers, implications and counterexamples
Scalars, vectors, matrices and tensor shape notation
Linear maps, matrix representations and composition
Span, independence, basis and change of coordinates
Column space, row space, null space and orthogonal complements
Rank, invertibility, solution sets and identifiability
Inner products, norms, angles and distance
Orthogonality, orthonormal bases and Gram-Schmidt
Projection matrices and residual geometry
Least squares, normal equations and stable solution routes
Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, diagonalization and spectral reasoning
Symmetric and positive-semidefinite matrices; Gram matrices
Singular-value decomposition and the pseudoinverse
PCA, low-rank approximation and reconstruction error
Batched shapes, broadcasting, parameter counts and operation costs
Condition number, residual error, solution error and numerical stability
Sparse and structured matrices
Advanced matrix perturbation theory

resources.name: MIT 18.06 - Linear Algebra
resources.use: Follow lectures 1-10, 14-17, 21-22, 25, 27, 29-31 and 33 with matching problems. This is the ordered first pass.

resources.name: MIT 6.042J - Proof strand
resources.use: Study textbook Chapters 1 and 3, §§4.1-4.4 and §§5.1-5.4 with matching Unit 1 problems. Leave the rest of the course.

resources.name: MIT 18.065 - Applied matrix bridge
resources.use: Use lectures 3-10 after 18.06 for SVD, PCA, low-rank approximation, matrix norms and solver difficulty.

resources.name: Mathematics for Machine Learning
resources.use: Use Chapters 2-4 and §10.2 to check notation or re-derive a result. Do not treat it as a second course.

resources.name: Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra
resources.use: Sample Chapters 1-13 and the extra exercises for computational practice in fitting, least squares and pseudoinverses.

resources.name: Essence of Linear Algebra
resources.use: Open only when a geometric picture is missing; it does not replace derivation or problem solving.

sections.checkpoint: Derive least squares and PCA, implement both from a blank file, and diagnose one rank-deficient or ill-conditioned case.
leaveForLater: Advanced matrix perturbation bounds
Specialized sparse-direct solvers
Functional analysis beyond what later tracks require

sections.title: Calculus & Automatic Differentiation
sections.why: Training is repeated differentiation through composed programs. Shape-aware derivatives and numerical checks are the fastest way to separate a wrong model from a wrong implementation.

topics.title: Limits, local approximation and differentiability
Partial and directional derivatives
Gradients as local linear models and steepest directions
Jacobians, Hessians and consistent shape conventions
First- and second-order Taylor approximations
Scalar and multivariable chain rule
Matrix derivatives for affine, quadratic and least-squares objectives
Gradients of logistic, softmax cross-entropy and regularized losses
Computational graphs and accumulation through branches
Forward mode, reverse mode, JVPs and VJPs
Backpropagation through dense layers and nonlinearities
Finite-difference gradient checking and its failure modes
Hessian-vector products
Implicit differentiation

resources.name: MIT 18.S096 - Matrix Calculus for ML
resources.use: Use lectures 1-5, the Hessian portion of lecture 7 and computational-graph portion of lecture 8; do the supplied problems and notebooks.

resources.name: Hands-On ML - Autodiff notebook
resources.use: Work through numerical differentiation and both AD modes, then rebuild the essential reverse-mode engine independently.

resources.name: PyTorch Autograd mechanics
resources.use: Consult after the handwritten engine for accumulation, graph behavior, disabled tracking and vector-Jacobian products.

resources.name: Mathematics for Machine Learning - Ch. 5
resources.use: Use Chapter 5 as the compact derivative, Jacobian, chain-rule and backpropagation reference.

resources.name: MIT 18.02SC - Multivariable Calculus Unit 2
resources.use: Use sessions 24-38 only if partial derivatives, gradients, Hessians or the multivariable chain rule are weak.

sections.checkpoint: Derive a branched matrix computation, implement a small reverse-mode autodiff engine, and isolate a seeded gradient error.
leaveForLater: General differential geometry
Full symbolic differentiation systems
Higher-order implicit differentiation

sections.title: Probability, Information & Bayesian Reasoning
sections.why: Model outputs, losses, sampling and uncertainty all depend on conditioning correctly and keeping the data-generating assumptions visible.

topics.title: Sample spaces, events and probability axioms
Random variables, PMFs, PDFs and CDFs
Joint, marginal and conditional distributions
Independence and conditional independence
Expectation, variance, covariance and correlation
Total probability, expectation and variance
Bernoulli, binomial, categorical, Gaussian, exponential and Poisson families
Transformations of random variables
Bayes rule, likelihood, evidence and posterior
Conditional expectation
Law of large numbers and central-limit behavior
Concentration bounds and what breaks under dependence or heavy tails
Monte Carlo estimation and sampling error
Entropy, cross-entropy, KL divergence and mutual information
Priors, conjugacy, posterior predictive distributions and sensitivity
Simple graphical factorization and latent variables
Measure-theoretic probability

resources.name: Harvard Stat 110 - Probability
resources.use: Follow lectures 4-14, 17-23 and 25-30 with matching Strategic Practice. Use lectures 1-3 only for prerequisite repair.

resources.name: Stat 110 Strategic Practice
resources.use: Solve the matching sets before marking a probability topic Practised; use solutions to audit reasoning, not to begin it.

resources.name: MIT 18.05 - Bayesian bridge
resources.use: Use classes 10-16 for MLE, Bayesian updating, posterior prediction, conjugacy, prior choice and credible intervals.

resources.name: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
resources.use: Consult targeted parts of Chapters 2, 3, 4 and 6 for ML notation, Monte Carlo, factorization, posterior prediction and information theory.

resources.name: D2L - Information Theory
resources.use: Use §§22.11.1-22.11.5 for runnable entropy, cross-entropy, KL and mutual-information examples and exercises.

sections.checkpoint: Solve a new conditional-probability problem, verify it by simulation, and derive a posterior predictive calculation with its assumptions.
leaveForLater: Measure-theoretic proofs
Advanced stochastic processes
General-purpose approximate inference

sections.title: Statistics, Experimentation & Causality
sections.why: A model result matters only when the estimand, uncertainty and decision rule survive leakage, selection and alternative explanations.

topics.title: Populations, samples, estimands, estimators and estimates
Bias, variance, consistency and efficiency
Likelihood, maximum likelihood and MAP estimation
Confidence, credible and prediction intervals
Hypothesis tests, errors, power and effect size
Bootstrap and permutation tests
Multiple comparisons, optional stopping and winner's curse
Regression assumptions and diagnostics
Calibration and uncertainty decomposition
Missingness and selection mechanisms
Randomization, units, metrics and experiment design
Power and minimum detectable effect
Predictive, associational and causal claims
Causal graphs, confounders, colliders and mediators
Interventions, adjustment and identification assumptions
Heterogeneous treatment effects
Semiparametric causal estimation

resources.name: MIT 14.310x - Data Analysis for Social Scientists
resources.use: Follow lectures 11-15, 17-20 and 22 with matching slides and problem sets for inference, regression, causality and experiment design.

resources.name: MIT 18.05 - Inference practice
resources.use: Use classes 17-20, 22-24 and 26 with their problem sets for tests, intervals, bootstrap and regression.

resources.name: Causal Inference: What If
resources.use: Read Chapters 1-3 and 6-8 for causal effects, DAGs, confounding, selection bias and identification reasoning.

resources.name: Patterns of trustworthy experimentation
resources.use: Read after the course to connect health checks, guardrails and statistical interpretation to production launch decisions.

resources.name: Always Valid Inference
resources.use: Use the introduction and worked motivation to understand optional-stopping failure. Reproducing the theory is outside this gate.

sections.checkpoint: Audit a flattering experiment, identify its validity failures, and produce a defensible rerun and decision memo.
leaveForLater: Advanced semiparametric efficiency theory
Longitudinal causal inference
Specialized survey methodology

sections.title: Optimization & Numerical Methods
sections.why: Training behavior is controlled by objective geometry, stochastic noise, finite precision and the state carried by the optimizer.

topics.title: Convex sets, convex functions and geometric intuition
First- and second-order optimality conditions
Smoothness, strong convexity and conditioning
Gradient descent on quadratic and general objectives
Stochastic gradients, minibatches and noise
Momentum and acceleration intuition
Adaptive optimizers, bias correction and weight decay
Learning-rate schedules, clipping and stopping
Constrained optimization, Lagrangians and KKT conditions
Regularization and proximal intuition
Floating-point representation, rounding and machine precision
Overflow, underflow and catastrophic cancellation
Stable softmax, log-sum-exp and online reductions
Residuals, tolerances and iterative-solver error
Mixed precision and accumulation choices
Newton and quasi-Newton methods
Convex duality beyond KKT interpretation

resources.name: Stanford EE364a - Convex Optimization
resources.use: Follow lectures 1-9 and 15-16; use lecture 17 only for KKT systems. Leave full interior-point treatment for later.

resources.name: Convex Optimization
resources.use: Read Chapters 1-5 and 9 with the course; use Chapter 10 only for equality-constrained Newton steps.

resources.name: D2L - Optimization Algorithms
resources.use: Use the convexity, GD, SGD, minibatch, momentum, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam and scheduler sections for ML derivations and code.

resources.name: Fundamentals of Numerical Computation
resources.use: Study §§1.1-1.4, 2.7-2.8, 3.2-3.4 and 4.2-4.3 for floating point, conditioning, stability, least squares and iteration error.

resources.name: CVXPY basic and DCP tutorials
resources.use: Use as the solver oracle after deriving a constrained problem and its KKT conditions by hand.

sections.checkpoint: Implement and compare optimizers on changed geometry, then diagnose one divergence and one finite-precision failure.
leaveForLater: Interior-point implementation details
Nonsmooth variational analysis
Large-scale distributed optimizer design

milestone.title: Numerical Learning Laboratory
milestone.description: Build a small NumPy project that connects least squares and PCA, reverse-mode differentiation, Monte Carlo uncertainty, experiment analysis and optimizer stability. Each component must include one failure case and one independent check.
deliverables: Derivations and assumption notes
Runnable implementation with tests and raw numerical comparisons
A short defense of solver, estimator and tolerance choices

stages.title: Programming & Software Engineering
stages.summary: Build reliable Python programs, explicit interfaces, reproducible tests, bounded concurrent services and safe native extensions.

sections.title: Python Execution Model
sections.why: Later ML code is still Python code. Precise reasoning about objects, imports, cleanup and package boundaries prevents silent state errors that framework knowledge cannot repair.

topics.title: Name binding, object identity and equality
Mutability, aliasing and visible state changes
Shallow and deep copying, hashability and dictionary key contracts
Argument binding, evaluation time and mutable defaults
Lexical scope, closures and captured state
Attribute lookup, class and instance state, and method binding
Core object protocols and deliberate dunder methods
Dataclasses, default factories, equality, ordering and frozen state
Iterable and iterator protocols, exhaustion and repeated iteration
Generators, lazy pipelines, send and cleanup behavior
Decorators, wrappers, metadata and parameterized decorators
Context managers, ownership and deterministic cleanup
Exception hierarchies, chaining, cleanup and actionable messages
Type hints, unions, generics, protocols and narrowing
Modules, packages, import resolution and module caching
Virtual environments, dependencies and editable installs
Src-layout packaging, pyproject metadata and console entry points
Reference counts, cycle collection and weak references
Custom descriptors and metaclass internals

resources.name: Stas' Python Cookbook - selected path
resources.use: Run Part I on dictionaries, iteration, functions, closures, decorators, classes and context managers; Part II on modules, files, paths, environment and arguments; and Part IV on versions, dependencies, packaging and code quality. Finish by building one src-layout package from a blank directory.

resources.name: Python language reference
resources.use: Check Data model, Execution model, Import system and Exceptions whenever a claim depends on Python semantics. These pages are the authority when the course and a runtime observation disagree.

resources.name: Packaging Python Projects
resources.use: Follow the packaging tutorial once from a blank directory, using a src layout, pyproject.toml, an isolated build and a clean-environment installation test.

resources.name: AlgoMaster Python - structured revision
resources.use: Use Functions, Modules and Packages, OOP, Advanced OOP, Exception Handling, Iterators and Generators, Type Hints and Annotations only after the cookbook pass. Open it for recall practice or a diagnosed weak mechanism, not as a second complete course.

sections.checkpoint: Build and install a typed src-layout package from a blank directory, then trace and repair one seeded aliasing, cleanup or import defect without trial-and-error edits.
leaveForLater: Metaclass frameworks and custom import hooks
CPython interpreter implementation details beyond a diagnosed need
Supporting multiple packaging backends

sections.title: Interfaces, Data & APIs
sections.why: Research and production systems fail at boundaries. Typed contracts, explicit schemas and idempotent interfaces keep malformed data and retries from becoming silent corruption.

topics.title: Nominal and structural typing, generics and protocols
Runtime validation and trusted versus untrusted boundaries
Typed configuration, precedence, secrets and unknown fields
JSON, JSONL and CSV encoding, null and numeric semantics
Schema versions, compatibility and explicit migrations
Bounded-memory ingestion and malformed-row quarantine
Columnar layout, Arrow and Parquet basics
Tables, keys, constraints and normalized relationships
Joins, aggregation, CTEs and window functions
Transactions, isolation anomalies and concurrency-sensitive invariants
Indexes, selectivity, cardinality and query plans
Backward-compatible migration, mixed versions and rollback
Domain, service, transport and persistence boundaries
Command-line inputs, output streams, exit codes and errors
HTTP methods, validation, status codes, pagination and streaming
Idempotency keys, duplicate replay and side-effect ownership
ORM identity maps, lazy loading and transaction boundaries
Distributed transactions and sagas

resources.name: Official docs typed-service build path
resources.provider: Python typing, Pydantic, FastAPI and PostgreSQL
resources.use: Build one record service in this order: structural protocols and generics; Pydantic models, validators, strict mode, serialization and settings; FastAPI request bodies, dependencies, errors and tests; then PostgreSQL transactions and EXPLAIN. Replay valid, malformed, duplicate and previous-schema requests through CLI and HTTP.

resources.name: AlgoMaster SQL - selected route
resources.use: Study SQL Foundations, Querying Data, Joins, Subqueries and CTEs, Window Functions, DDL, DML and Views, Performance Optimization, Transactions and Concurrency, and Data Modeling. Stop when the service queries and transaction tests pass.

resources.name: PostgreSQL transactions and EXPLAIN
resources.use: Use the transaction tutorial and EXPLAIN guide to demonstrate commit, rollback, one isolation anomaly or prevented anomaly, and a measured plan improvement on the database actually used.

resources.name: FastAPI tutorial
resources.use: Use Request Body, Dependencies, Handling Errors and Testing to expose the same service layer through HTTP. Keep framework models outside the domain core and preserve the same error semantics as the CLI.

resources.name: AlgoMaster Low-Level Design - one rehearsal
resources.use: Use one fitting design prompt to rehearse interface contracts, dependency direction and failure ownership. Treat the review as feedback, then verify behavior with your own tests.

resources.name: Stas' Python Cookbook - data and interfaces
resources.use: Use Serialization and Deserialization plus Environment and Arguments for focused implementation help. Compare JSON, JSONL, CSV and compressed data, and never use pickle for untrusted interchange.

sections.checkpoint: Expose one typed service through CLI and HTTP, ingest malformed and old-version records safely, and defend the schema, transaction and idempotency boundaries.
leaveForLater: Large web frameworks and frontend development
Distributed databases and cross-service transactions
ORM-specific architecture beyond one small comparison

sections.title: Testing, Debugging & Reproducibility
sections.why: Correctness claims need an independent oracle and failures need evidence. This section turns testing, source control and environment capture into one repeatable investigation discipline.

topics.title: Unit, contract, integration, end-to-end and performance tests
Requirements, invariants, independent oracles and boundary cases
Fixtures, fakes, stubs, mocks and integration risk
Property, metamorphic and differential testing
Regression tests and targeted failure injection
Randomness, time, concurrency, external state and flaky tests
Generated cases, shrinking and durable failure replay
Debugger, logs, traces and minimum distinguishing observations
Competing hypotheses, evidence and root-cause notes
Shell quoting, streams, exit status, signals and partial output
Permissions, environment, processes, file descriptors and logs
Commits, branches, merges, rebases and detached state
Bisect, reflog and preservation-first recovery
SSH trust, keys, forwarding and durable tmux sessions
Dependency locks, clean environments and repeatable builds
Data identity, configuration, seeds, manifests and checksums
Type, lint, test, build and installation gates
Hermetic builds and reproducible-build guarantees

resources.name: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education
resources.use: Complete the 2026 lectures on the shell, command-line environment, development tools, debugging and profiling, Git, packaging and shipping code, and code quality. Apply every exercise to the same stage project.

resources.name: pytest documentation
resources.use: Use Get Started, fixtures, parametrization, monkeypatch, caplog and temporary paths to build behavior and failure-path tests without order dependence.

resources.name: Hypothesis documentation
resources.use: Follow the Quick start and property-based testing guides, then generate operation histories and retain the minimized example for one real defect.

resources.name: The Art of Debugging
resources.use: Use the Unix, Python and compiled-code sections during a real seeded defect. Follow the evidence and tiny-reproducer workflow rather than reading the unfinished book front to back.

resources.name: Pro Git
resources.use: Use Chapters 2-3 and the sections on debugging, internals and recovery while constructing a history for bisect and recovering a deliberately displaced commit.

resources.name: Stas' Python Cookbook - debugging and testing
resources.use: Use Part III and the packaging sections for debugger, traceback, pytest, logging, profiling and clean-environment recipes.

sections.checkpoint: Resolve one unfamiliar seeded defect with a hypothesis log and regression test, then rebuild and reproduce the result from a clean checkout and recover one displaced Git commit.
leaveForLater: Organization-wide CI platform administration
Formal verification systems
Reproducible builds across every operating system

sections.title: Concurrency, Profiling & Operations
sections.why: A fast happy path is not an operable system. Bounded work, cancellation, profiles and observable failure behavior are the foundations for later training and serving systems.

topics.title: CPU-bound, I/O-bound, stateful and cancellation-sensitive work
Threads, processes and asynchronous tasks
Python GIL implications and extension-code release boundaries
Locks, semaphores, conditions, events and queues
Race, deadlock, livelock, starvation and lost wakeups
Task ownership, task groups, cancellation and cleanup
Timeouts, deadlines, retry budgets, jitter and idempotency
Bounded queues, admission control, backpressure and load shedding
Signals, graceful shutdown and partial-work disposition
Sampling versus instrumentation and wall versus CPU time
CPU profiles, allocation traces, RSS and memory retention
Warmup, repeated trials, workload control and raw results
Structured logs, correlation IDs and secret redaction
Low-cardinality metrics, latency distributions and queue depth
Trace context, spans and cross-boundary latency
Readiness, liveness and dependency health
Container builds, non-root execution, limits and signals
Process supervision and diagnosis runbooks
eBPF and kernel-level production tracing

resources.name: AlgoMaster Concurrency
resources.use: Study Concurrency 101; the Python units on threads, the GIL, multiprocessing, asyncio and concurrent.futures; synchronization primitives; concurrency challenges; locking strategies; and concurrency patterns. Then solve Bounded Buffer, Thread-Safe Blocking Queue, Thread-Safe Rate Limiter and Task Scheduler with Dependencies.

resources.name: Python concurrency documentation
resources.use: Use asyncio task groups, cancellation, queues and timeouts; concurrent.futures; multiprocessing; threading; and signal documentation to verify lifecycle and failure behavior.

resources.name: High Performance Python, 3rd edition
resources.provider: Micha Gorelick and Ian Ozsvald, O'Reilly
resources.use: Read Chapter 2 Profiling to Find Bottlenecks, Chapter 9 Asynchronous I/O, Chapter 10 The multiprocessing Module and Chapter 12 Using Less RAM, and use the companion code (github.com/mynameisfiber/high_performance_python_3e) as experiment starting points. Change the workloads and measure the regimes where concurrency helps, loses or only moves the bottleneck.

resources.name: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces - concurrency
resources.use: Read Chapters 26-33, from threads through event-based concurrency, for locks, condition variables, semaphores, concurrency bugs and event loops. Do selected homework only for a weak mechanism.

resources.name: Docker guides
resources.use: Use the Python container guide and build best practices to run as non-root, pin dependencies, handle signals and test CPU and memory limits.

resources.name: OpenTelemetry Python instrumentation
resources.use: Manually instrument one request so its structured logs, one low-cardinality metric and one trace share a correlation identity. Use the telemetry to locate one seeded fault.

sections.checkpoint: Run a bounded worker pipeline through overload, cancellation and worker failure, then use profiles, logs and metrics to justify one measured improvement and one rejected optimization.
leaveForLater: Cluster orchestration and service meshes
Kernel tracing beyond a concrete diagnosis
Organization-scale observability platforms

sections.title: C & C++ Systems Literacy
sections.why: GPU kernels, runtimes and Python extensions cross native boundaries. You need enough layout, lifetime and build fluency to make a safe bounded change and understand the resulting machine behavior.

topics.title: Preprocess, compile, assemble, link, load and symbols
Warnings, debug symbols, optimization and ABI compatibility
Integer representation, conversions and overflow
Pointers, references, arrays and explicit spans
Struct and class layout, padding, alignment and strides
Stack and heap storage duration and allocation
RAII, ownership and smart pointers
Copy, move and object lifetime through exceptions
Templates and generic code at reading depth
Container, iterator and invalidation contracts
Out-of-bounds, lifetime, uninitialized access and undefined behavior
Compiler diagnostics, sanitizers and debugger evidence
Threads, data races, memory ordering and atomics at literacy depth
Contiguous layout, locality, array of structures and structure of arrays
Python/native dtype, shape, stride, ownership, GIL and error contracts
Repeatable CMake configure, build and test targets
C linkage and stable foreign-function boundaries
Advanced template metaprogramming

resources.name: AlgoMaster C++
resources.use: Use the sections on compilation, pointers and references, memory, RAII and smart pointers, copy and move, STL containers, templates, errors, concurrency and paired exercises. Skip competitive-programming breadth already covered in Algorithms.

resources.name: C++ Core Guidelines
resources.use: Use the Philosophy, Interfaces, Resource management, Expressions, Containers and concurrency rule groups to review ownership and safety decisions in the native component.

resources.name: cppreference
resources.use: Consult language lifetime, object model, value categories, memory model, atomics, containers and iterator invalidation while reading or modifying code.

resources.name: Clang AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
resources.use: Compile seeded memory defects with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, preserve the reports, repair the root cause and keep regression tests.

resources.name: pybind11 documentation
resources.use: Follow First steps and NumPy support to expose one small native function with explicit shape, dtype, stride, ownership, GIL and exception behavior.

resources.name: CMake tutorial
resources.use: Use the introductory steps for targets, libraries, testing and install rules. Produce one clean debug build and one optimized build without copied one-off commands.

sections.checkpoint: Build a tiny Python-callable C++ component, explain its layout and ownership, and repair one seeded lifetime or bounds error from sanitizer evidence in a clean build.
leaveForLater: Advanced template metaprogramming and compiler construction
Large native application architecture
Lock-free data structures beyond literacy

milestone.title: Reproducible Task Runner
milestone.description: Review the stage through three small artifacts drawn from the Python Experimental Systems Kit. Keep them in one repository so each artifact strengthens the same system instead of becoming a separate project.
deliverables: Package and interface - typed installable service through CLI and HTTP, with schema and transaction tests
Failure and operations - bounded concurrency, backpressure, cancellation, telemetry, one injected failure and a clean-checkout runbook
Native and diagnosis - one Python-native function, a sanitizer-backed repair and one evidence-first debugging report

stages.title: Algorithms & Data Structures
stages.summary: Choose representations from constraints, derive invariants and proofs, implement reliable algorithms, and test them against adversarial cases.

sections.title: Complexity & Linear Structures
sections.why: The first algorithmic skill is translating constraints into a cost budget and preserving a simple invariant. Arrays, hashing, windows and queues expose these habits with minimal abstraction.

topics.title: Input size, operation model and resource budget
Big O, Theta and Omega with stated variables
Worst, average, expected and output-sensitive cost
Aggregate, accounting and amortized reasoning
Loop invariants, initialization, maintenance and termination
Arrays, strings, contiguous layout and locality
Singly and doubly linked structures and pointer invariants
Hashing, collisions, load factor, resizing and tombstones
Stacks, queues, circular buffers and deques
Two-pointer invariants and ordering assumptions
Fixed and variable windows and monotonicity
Prefix sums, difference arrays and prefix plus hash
Monotone stacks and deques
Brute-force oracles and randomized differential tests
Potential-function amortized proofs
Adversarial and cryptographic hashing

resources.name: DSA Handbook - Foundations and linear patterns
resources.use: Study Part 0, Part 1, Part 3 and Part 4 in order. Use the routing-rule pages for arrays versus lists, map choice, stack versus queue, two pointers, sliding windows and prefix methods before seeing solved code.

resources.name: AlgoMaster DSA - linear structures slice
resources.use: Attempt Design HashMap, Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters and Sliding Window Maximum cold. Hide tags, state the invariant first, and add randomized operation histories to Design HashMap.

resources.name: MIT 6.042J - asymptotics and invariants
resources.use: Use the asymptotics, state-machine invariants and proof-method readings when a cost or correctness argument is weak. Solve only the matching problems.

resources.name: Algorithmica - memory and data layout
resources.use: Read the memory hierarchy, cache and complexity-model chapters, then measure one contiguous-versus-linked and one hash-versus-ordered workload crossover.

resources.name: NeetCode - unseen linear problems
resources.use: Use only for two tag-hidden transfer problems after the AlgoMaster slice. Do not start another full roadmap or watch a solution before the attempt is complete.

sections.checkpoint: Solve two tag-hidden linear-structure problems, state each invariant before coding, and use randomized tests to expose and minimize one plausible wrong solution.
leaveForLater: Cryptographic and learned hashing
Persistent and concurrent collections
Specialized succinct data structures

sections.title: Search, Sorting, Trees & Heaps
sections.why: Ordered structure turns brute force into logarithmic search, efficient selection and hierarchical state. The gain is reliable only when boundaries and representation invariants are explicit.

Stable merge sort and divide-combine reasoning

Trie representation, prefix lookup and memory cost
Interval ordering, merging and sweep reasoning
Ranks, order statistics and augmented trees
B-trees, suffix structures and persistent search trees

resources.name: DSA Handbook - search, trees and heaps
resources.use: Study Part 2 Search and Sort, Part 5 Linked Lists, and Part 6 Trees and Heaps. Include canonical and answer-space binary search, comparison and linear-time sorts, quickselect, sentinels, cycles, heaps, BSTs, balanced-tree vocabulary, tries and segment trees.

resources.name: AlgoMaster DSA - ordered structures slice
resources.use: Attempt Koko Eating Bananas, Validate Binary Search Tree and Find Median from Data Stream cold. Use Merge Intervals only if interval modeling remains weak, and include duplicate-heavy and skewed inputs.

resources.name: Algorithmica - search and sorting performance
resources.use: Use the binary-search, sorting, branch prediction and cache chapters to explain why two algorithms with the same asymptotic bound cross over on real workloads.

resources.name: Algorithms
resources.use: Use the recursion and divide-and-conquer chapters when deriving merge, partition and selection algorithms. This is the proof reference when the handbook explanation is too brief.

resources.name: NeetCode - unseen ordered problems
resources.use: Use one unseen tree problem and one heap or interval problem as the final transfer check, with solution material closed until submission.

sections.checkpoint: Derive one binary-search boundary without patching it by examples, then solve one unseen tree and one heap or interval problem with adversarial tests and a worst-case defense.
leaveForLater: Implementing every balanced-tree variant
External-memory and database index internals
Advanced suffix trees and compressed indexes

sections.title: Graph Modeling & Algorithms
sections.why: Many scheduling, dependency, routing and state-transition problems are graphs before they are algorithms. Correct modeling and assumption checks matter more than recalling a traversal name.

Adjacency lists, matrices, edge lists and implicit graphs
BFS frontier invariant and unweighted shortest paths

Connected components and reachability

Strongly connected components
Union-find, path compression and union by rank or size

resources.name: DSA Handbook - graphs
resources.use: Study all of Part 8 in order. For each algorithm, write the representation, invariant, forbidden input assumptions and independently checkable output before reading the implementation.

resources.name: AlgoMaster DSA - graph slice
resources.use: Attempt Number of Islands, Course Schedule and Network Delay Time cold. They cover traversal, dependency modeling and weighted shortest paths; add one narrative problem only if graph modeling remains weak.

resources.name: Algorithms - graph chapters
resources.use: Use the basic graph, minimum spanning tree, shortest path and flow chapters for correctness proofs and counterexamples to tempting wrong algorithms.

resources.name: Hypothesis - generated graph tests
resources.use: Generate small sparse, dense, disconnected, cyclic, parallel-edge and weighted graphs. Compare optimized results with exhaustive or deliberately simple references and retain shrunk failures.

resources.name: NeetCode - unseen graph problems
resources.use: Use two unseen story problems without graph tags. Grade the model, assumptions, certificate and tests as well as the final answer.

sections.checkpoint: Convert two unfamiliar narratives into graphs, implement the selected algorithms with certificates, and reject one wrong method using a minimized counterexample.
leaveForLater: Full maximum-flow and matching implementation families
Spectral and geometric graph algorithms
Large-scale graph processing frameworks

sections.title: Decomposition, Greedy Methods & Randomness
sections.why: Hard problems often become manageable by exposing recursive state, proving a local choice, or accepting a controlled probability. Each shortcut needs a proof boundary and an adversarial test.

topics.title: Recursive state, base cases and return contracts
Choice, unchoice and complete search
